event.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 27?
event.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 27 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official meteorological observations from Munich-area stations, including Munich International Airport, recorded a peak air temperature of 30°C during the afternoon of August 27 under partly cloudy skies and light easterly winds associated with a stable high-pressure ridge. This value aligned precisely with model consensus from sources such as the GFS, which forecasted afternoon maxima near 30–31°C given the season’s typical insolation and minimal cloud cover inhibiting radiative cooling. Trader consensus at 100% for 30°C reflects real-time station data and the absence of any upward revisions in official reporting, consistent with the day’s measured range of roughly 14–30°C. Only an unexpected post-analysis correction from the Deutscher Wetterdienst or equivalent authority could alter resolution, though such adjustments remain rare once hourly maxima are confirmed.
